_notes: Compiled by Tom Collins, based on st_162h by HorsePin
player_count added at 0x02110900, the one address shared across every Stern SAM game checked --
24, X-Men, LUCI and both Star Trek revisions, over ten captures at one, two and four players.
The declared score slots were confirmed on hardware rather than assumed: a 4-player game ending
1,236,620 / 2,197,850 / 1,137,910 / 1,714,440 read back exactly at 0x02110A0C on a 4-byte stride.
current_player and current_ball are still unmapped. Neither is retained in NVRAM after a game,
and a sweep of 0x0-0x3FFFF did not produce the adjacent pair that identified them on X-Men and
LUCI, so they are somewhere else in CPU RAM.
current_player/current_ball came from the joint pair test -- the player wrapping to 1 in the same
sample the ball steps up -- which returned exactly one hit across a full four-player game.
Unlike trn_174h and twd_156c, this ROM resets both counters to 1 at game end, so its exit dump
reads 1/1 rather than the 4/3 that confirmed those two. The single in-play hit is the evidence
here; the dump neither confirms nor contradicts it.
Scores verified against the same dump: 2,032,370 / 1,248,620 / 1,330,340 / 1,342,740 at 4-byte
centres from 0x02110A0C, where stride 8 runs into the 0xFFFFFFFF fill. The sweep independently
reproduced this map's existing score address, and rejected a CPU RAM candidate at 0x00038D9C
whose four values (~16.7M, near-identical) are the usual scaled-set false positive.
game_over, credits, max_credits and ball_count come from a 765-frame recording of live memory
spanning an operator-menu session and a full game, captured about twice a second.
game_over at 0x0003BA3E holds exactly two values across the recording, 0 while a game runs and 1
in attract, matching the true state in all 765 frames. Note it also reads 0 while the operator
menu is open, so 'in the menu' looks like 'in a game'; that is harmless for edge detection but
it is not a general 'no game in progress' flag.
It is NOT at a fixed offset from current_ball. trn_174h keeps its equivalent 0x31 bytes past the
ball counter and encoded differently (19 in game, 1 otherwise); the byte at that offset here
takes five values and is unrelated. This field has to be measured per ROM.
ball_count and max_credits were identified by setting them to distinctive values in the operator
menu -- 5 balls and 9 credits -- so the changed records named themselves: index 32 went 3 to 5
and index 34 went 30 to 9 in the adjustment array. Both check bytes validate.
credits at 0x0211100C rose 0,1,3,4,6 as credits were added in the menu and fell to 5 when the
game started. 0x02111008 carries the fractional part (the machine showed 6.5), and 0x0211100D
moves inversely but is not a plain complement of the value, so no checksum is declared for it.
tilted at 0x0003310B, from the same recording: the machine was tilted on ball 1. The byte is set
at frame 209 and clears when ball 2 starts, and it is never set at any other point in the
recording. What confirms it is a signal not used to find it -- player 1's score rises steadily
through 88,330 and freezes on the exact frame the byte sets, staying frozen until the ball ends,
which is what a tilt does and a ball-in-play flag does not.
A single-frame blip at 204, while scoring was still rising, is a tilt warning rather than the
tilt itself.
Only one tilt was observed, so this is one event corroborated by the score rather than a repeated
pattern.
2026-11: game_over and tilted read the status byte 0x00034156 (01 attract, 7B/99/8C/14 play, 16
tilted). 0x0003BA3E reads 0 after power-up until a game has ended, and 0x0003310B is also set
for a moment at each tilt warning.
2026-11: Master Volume and the A.1 (64) and A.2 (51) adjustments added from the ROM image
(README, 'Adjustments from the ROM').
Confirmed on a cabinet 2026-11-13 (ALP4K; two games, tilt on P1 ball 1): 784,350 / 1,127,220 and
1,003,230 / 1,612,600, the records and the status byte matched the DMD.
